turns.t: Morning, doctor. My diabetes check is due, but I also get tingling in my feet now, and I wanted to ask about that.
Good morning. Let's start with the tingling. Which part of the feet?
The toes, mostly, on both sides. Like pins and needles.
When did you first notice it?
Oh, I couldn't say. Maybe the spring? Or last winter. I really don't remember.
Is it there all the time, or does it come and go?
It's worse in the evening, when I'm sitting down.
Any weakness in the legs, or falls?
No, nothing like that. My legs feel strong.
Tell me about the diabetes medicines you're on.
Metformin, 500 mg, twice a day. Then a small yellow one in the morning, I don't know the name. And the injection at night.
Do you know how many units of the injection you take?
Twenty, I think. Or perhaps twenty-four. My wife does it, she writes it down.
I'll ask you to bring her diary next time, then we'll be sure. Any other conditions besides the diabetes?
Diabetes, for about ten years. That's all, really.
Have you noticed any trouble with your eyes, or sores on your feet?
No. My eyes are fine, and my feet have no sores.
Good. I'll check your pulse, blood pressure and weight now. ~
Go ahead. ~
Pulse 74, blood pressure 134 over 80, weight 88 kilograms, temperature 36.6.
Is the weight all right? ~
It's about the same as last visit. I'd like to test the sensation in your feet with a thread in a moment. ~
Does it hurt? ~
Not at all. Just tell me when you feel it. ~
Yes. Yes. Hmm, I didn't feel that one. ~
Thank you. I'd like to send blood tests for your sugar control, the HbA1c, and also your kidneys and B12.
All right. ~
The tingling may well be early nerve damage from the diabetes, but I'd like the tests to say so.
Is it serious? ~
It's common, and it often settles when the sugars are steady. Please check your feet daily, and wear shoes that fit well.
I will. ~
Come back in three weeks with your wife's diary, and I'll go through the results with you.
Three weeks. Thank you, doctor. ~
